title: Manifest
description:
How to install one package.

`deny_unknown_fields` is deliberate: a manifest is hand-written, often by
someone else, and a misspelt key that is silently ignored produces a package
that installs the wrong thing with no complaint anywhere.

asset.description: Narrows which release asset is chosen.

bin.description: Which executables to link, and under what names. Empty means discover.

description.description: One line, shown by `ketch info` and `ketch search`.

extra_paths.description:
Man pages and completions to expose from the payload. A string is
classified by the path rules in `docs/MANIFESTS.md`; a table sets `kind`.

hooks.description: Commands to run around install, update and uninstall. See `crate::hooks`.

name.description:
The install name: a directory in the store and the key in
`state.json`. A registry package folder supplies it; elsewhere it is
required.

provides.description: Alternate names this package answers to.

strip_prefix.description: Leading path components to drop when extracting.

trust.description: Whose signature a release must carry. See `crate::trust`.

$comment: Generated from the Rust types by `KETCH_BLESS=1 cargo nextest run schema`. Do not edit.

AssetSelector.description: Which release asset to pick. Empty means "let the platform decide".

exclude.description: Asset must match none of these.

include.description: Asset must match at least one of these (glob: `*` and `?`).

target.description:
Per-target override, keyed by `TargetSpec` display form, e.g.
`"macos-aarch64" = "*-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"`.

BinSpec.description: One executable to expose on PATH.

name.description: Name of the symlink. Defaults to the file name of `path`.

path.description:
Path inside the extracted payload. Globs allowed; when a glob matches
several files, the one whose stem is `name` is linked. When absent,
ketch discovers executables automatically.

CompletionShell.description: Shell whose user completion directory an extra path should land in.

ExtraKind.description:
What an `extra_paths` entry is for. Required in the table form; inferred
from path rules when the entry is a bare string.

oneOf.description: A man page, linked into the user man root.
A shell completion script, linked into that shell's user directory.

ExtraPath.description: One `extra_paths` entry: a payload-relative string, or a table with `kind`.

anyOf.description: Classified by the path rules in `docs/MANIFESTS.md`.
Explicit kind; path rules are not consulted except to fill `shell`/`section`.

ExtraPathSpec.description: Table form of `extra_paths`: an explicit kind, so path rules are not guessed.

path.description: Path inside the extracted payload. Same containment rules as a string entry.

section.description: Man section (`1`, `8`, `1p`). Inferred from a `*.N` file name when absent.

shell.description: Required for a completion when the file name does not name a shell.

Hooks.description:
Commands a manifest runs around its own install, update and uninstall.

Each is one line for the platform shell. `crate::hooks` runs them, and
only from a manifest in the user's own manifest directory: anywhere else
the manifest is someone else's file, and a command in it is their code.

oneOf.description: Decide from what the payload actually contains.
Command-line executables linked into the bin dir.
A macOS `.app` bundle placed in the applications dir.

PackageRef.description: `scheme:id` (`github:BurntSushi/ripgrep`, `myplugin:some-id`), or a bare `owner/repo`, which means GitHub.

TrustMode.description: What an unverifiable signature does to the install.

oneOf.description: Install on the checksum alone, and say so.

TrustPolicy.description:
A manifest's `trust` table: whose signature a release must carry.

Which keys a verifier reads is checked by `crate::trust::check_policy`,
called from [`Manifest::validate`]; `docs/MANIFESTS.md` is the reference.

fingerprint.description: gpg: the primary key's full fingerprint.

issuer.description: sigstore: the OIDC issuer of the signing certificate.

public_key.description: minisign: the key. gpg: the armored key block.

repository.description: sigstore: any GitHub Actions workflow in this `owner/repo`.

signature.description: The sidecar's name; `{file}` is the signed file's name.

signed.description: A glob naming a checksum list the signature covers instead of the asset.

Verifier.description: Which kind of publisher signature a `trust` table asks for.
